title: The Book That Never Left
premise_public: Just after midnight, a librarian's phone reported that a book had been borrowed. The building had been locked for hours, nobody had entered, and the printed copy was still on its shelf. The checkout record was accurate.
solution_summary: The library's shared catalogue grouped its printed and electronic editions under one title. A patron borrowed the electronic edition through the library app from home after midnight. The alert referred to that digital loan, while the shelf copy never moved.

facts.text: The catalogue grouped a printed edition and a licensed electronic edition under one title.
A patron could borrow through the library app without entering the building.
The after-midnight checkout was for an electronic edition rather than the printed book.
The printed copy remained on its shelf, which did not contradict the title-level alert.
The circulation alert and security records were both accurate.

acceptable_solutions: The library app let someone borrow an ebook from home, while the printed book stayed on the shelf.
A digital edition was checked out through the shared library catalogue after hours, not the physical copy.
The record was for an electronic loan made remotely and the print edition never moved.
hints: The record identifies a title, not necessarily the object on the shelf.
Think about whether every kind of library loan requires entering the building.
